answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens along an execution thread, audited via topological cut verifications. Honest nodes challenge anomalies; if an audit detects a fraudulent state delta, the colluding cluster faces stake slashing. Randomly sampling small sparrow nodes to verify graph cuts imposes superlinear attacker cost O(N^2) relative to cluster size, making mass counterfeit identities mathematically unprofitable.
